title: intend --extract-from: arrive with action records and intent insight
description:
# Gathering (dossier document-view)

Self-description: intend should not start from a blank page when the work already has a trail. `--extract-from` names the items to read first. Beads and epics are the usual items. The agent shows up with records of action and insight into the intent those records imply. Other resources (images, articles, ADRs, pastes, sketches) are bundled as a dossier — the gathering already named in ADR-007 — not as a ninth kind or a fourth store.

This intention emerged from that gathering. The gathering is not consumed.

## Citations

- Epic `bazaar-db8` and children (especially `.1` folded ADR-007, `.3` gather, `.4` promote still titled as 1:1 consume)
- `openspec/specs/dossier/spec.md` — emerge with provenance; gathering stays
- `openspec/specs/verbs/spec.md` — intend observes living specs, in-flight, LEARNINGS; no extract-from yet
- `plugins/intention/skills/intend/SKILL.md` — observe step is blank-page
- `plugins/intention/references/intend-dag.md` — no Extract section
- ADR-007, ADR-008 (`ARCHITECTURE.md`)
- `docs/LEARNINGS.md` — 1:1 “dossier becomes a Project” failed advise
- `openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-17-add-dossier-objects/proposal.md` — promote id means emerge, not consume
- In-flight leftover: `openspec/changes/add-run-verb/` still ACTIVE BUILD after archive (not this intention)
- Open: `bazaar-ja7` (bytes; blocks gather), `bazaar-db8.2` host, `bazaar-db8.5` UI

## Insight already on the trail

Dossier is the bundle. Gather records citations; promote is emerge-with-cite, not rename-into-a-project. Extract-from is the intend face of that emerge when the source is a dossier, and the usual face when the source is beads/epics.

## Intention

`--extract-from` on intend. Usual items: beads/epics. Output of observe: action records + insight into intent. Dossier bundles other relevant resources. Record this intention (done here).
acceptance_criteria:

A dossier is a valid extract-from item once gather exists; emerged work cites the dossier and does not consume it.
This intention is recorded and cites the gathering (ADR-007).

title: nod-edge-source: decide where the host's edges come from
description:
Split out of bazaar-lgr.5. That bead conflated a decision with an implementation, and the decision is the part that needs a human.

The living spec (openspec/specs/taskmaster) already SHALLs 'ready is derived, never stored' — and graph.ts DOES derive correctly. The failure is not the derivation, it is that the EDGE SET is a hand-copied fiction. So the open question is narrow and worth naming precisely: where does a host legitimately obtain kernel state?

Options, rising cost:
  a) Export — kernel writes .beads to JSON, app repo vendors it, guest pulls on deploy. No new interface. Stale between pulls.
  b) Endpoint — kernel serves ready-set JSON, host fetches live. This is a NEW cross-repo interface and therefore escalates this node to architecture: ADR + Grok as independent reader.
  c) bd replica on the guest. Most live, duplicates the source of truth, and risks the parallel kernel the taskmaster spec forbids.

Decide, name the rejected options and why, and only then hand to bazaar-lgr.5.
design:
Escalation trigger: choosing (b) makes this architecture rigor — it defines how any host reads kernel truth, which is precedent, not plumbing. (a) and (c) are change rigor.

Constraint from the living spec: whatever the transport, no stored ready column and no Taskmaster-only object model. If the host needs a field the packet lacks, amend docs/contracts/agent-surface.md instead.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] One option chosen, in writing, with the rejected ones named and why
[ ] If (b): an ADR exists and Grok has read it as an independent reader
[ ] No stored ready flag introduced by the choice
[ ] bazaar-lgr.5 can start without further discussion
close_reason:
Decided: exported snapshot, pulled at deploy time. Change: openspec/changes/add-taskmaster-edge-source (ACTIVE BUILD).

[x] One option chosen in writing, rejected ones named and why — design.md records (b) live endpoint, (c) bd replica on guest, (d) raw fetch from forge, each with the reason it lost.
[x] Escalation NOT triggered — (b) was the trigger and was rejected, so no ADR and no Grok reader; rigor stayed change.
[x] No stored ready flag; readySet() unchanged, and the contract carries no 'ready' field.
[x] bazaar-lgr.5 can start — JSON contract (shape + required generated_at) is fixed in design.md.

Load-bearing clause: the host must STATE the age of the snapshot it derives from. The original defect was not that data was old, it was that the page did not say so. Spec delta makes silence non-conformant.

title: nod-live-graph: the ready set reads real state, not a hand-synced file
description:
Promotes ghost T1b. `src/lib/graph.ts` is a hand-maintained seed and it has already gone stale in production: on 2026-08-16 it showed bazaar-lgr.3 as open hours after it closed, so the page put finished work at the top of READY in signal colour and hid bazaar-lgr.4 — genuinely startable — under WAITING at 0.62 opacity.

The product's one job is 'what can I start'. A hand-synced graph cannot do that job, and every hour the file drifts the site is lying in the confident voice we designed for it. This is the single highest-value open node on taskmaster.dev.

Either wire it to real state, or delete the footer's claim that the graph is this project's own work. Truth or humility — the current third option is the bug.
design:
# bazaar-lgr.5: the ready set reads a dated export, not GRAPH[]

**Goal.** `/` derives from `docs/taskmaster/graph.json` (vendored at
deploy). Close a bead, re-export, pull the guest — that id leaves READY
without a hand edit of `graph.ts`. The page states `generated_at`. A
bad snapshot paints empty and says why.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `/` is computed from the vendored snapshot, not `GRAPH` in `graph.ts`
- [ ] A node `closed` in `bd` then re-exported is `landed` (not READY) after the guest pulls
- [ ] `readySet()` still derives `open ∧ every needs id is landed`; no `ready` field anywhere
- [ ] Page states snapshot age wherever a ready set is shown (`as of <generated_at>`)
- [ ] Absent / unparseable / missing `generated_at` → empty ready set + the reason; never fall back to the seed
- [ ] WARNING comment and the `GRAPH` seed are gone
- [ ] Still one process, one SQLite; no new table

## Contract
Producer (already landed in the bazaar — do not rewrite):

```
python3 scripts/export-graph.py
# writes docs/taskmaster/graph.json
```

Shape (from `openspec/changes/archive/2026-08-16-add-taskmaster-edge-source/design.md`):

```json
{
  "generated_at": "2026-08-16T16:40:00Z",
  "source": "bazaar",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "bazaar-lgr.4",
      "title": "add-taskmaster-host — kernel ADR names the host",
      "kind": "node",
      "state": "open",
      "needs": ["bazaar-lgr.3"]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `state` is `open` | `landed`. Closed → `landed`. Deferred/parked omitted.
- `needs` contains only ids present in `nodes`.
- No `ready` key on the document or any node.
- Missing `generated_at` ⇒ unusable.

Seam already in the app (`src/lib/graph.ts`):

```ts
export function readySet(g: WorkNode[] = GRAPH): WorkNode[]
// keep the function; stop defaulting to a seed
```

There is no `+page.server.ts`. Load today is look/visit in
`src/routes/+layout.server.ts`. Put snapshot load in a new
`+page.server.ts` so the layout stays cookies-only. `#lib`, not `$lib`.

## Inherited
- Hand-synced `GRAPH` already lied: `lgr.3` stayed open on READY, hid `lgr.4` (NOTES; `graph.ts` WARNING).
- Ready is derived, never stored (ADR-006 / living `taskmaster` spec).
- Transport is export-at-deploy, not a live endpoint, not `bd` on the guest (`bazaar-lgr.11` closed).
- `bd list` hides closed issues — export uses `bd list --all` (LEARNINGS).
- CSS/HMR lies: after a visual change, `systemctl restart taskmaster-dev`, not a reload (NOTES).
- Guest git needs `core.sshCommand=/usr/local/bin/tm-git-ssh`.

## Out of scope
- Footer humility copy — `bazaar-lgr.12` (superseded once `as of` exists; do not do it here)
- Eyebrow “6 nodes resolved” — `bazaar-lgr.10` (blocked on this bead)
- Live kernel endpoint / `bd` replica / GitHub fetch — rejected in edge-source design
- IdentiKey, groups (T1c), Playwright-in-VM (T1d), scaffold/favicon/404 (`.6` `.7` `.8`)
- Folding `add-taskmaster-live-graph` or changing `export-graph.py`
- New drizzle tables (the leftover `task` table is not this node)
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] `/` is computed from the vendored snapshot, not GRAPH in graph.ts
[ ] A node closed in bd then re-exported is landed (not READY) after the guest pulls
[ ] readySet() still derives open ∧ every needs id is landed; no ready field anywhere
[ ] Page states snapshot age wherever a ready set is shown (as of <generated_at>)
[ ] Absent / unparseable / missing generated_at → empty ready set + the reason; never fall back to the seed
[ ] WARNING comment and the GRAPH seed are gone
[ ] Still one process, one SQLite; no new table
notes:
2026-08-16 — unblocked. Transport decided in openspec/changes/add-taskmaster-edge-source (bazaar-lgr.11 closed): exported snapshot pulled at deploy, NOT a live endpoint.

The JSON contract is fixed in that change's design.md — shape, state mapping (closed→landed), no dangling edges, and a REQUIRED generated_at. Build against it, do not re-derive it.

Two clauses from the spec delta that are acceptance, not advice:
  - the page must STATE the snapshot's age wherever it shows a ready set
  - a missing/unparseable/undated snapshot renders EMPTY with the reason — never a fallback to the seeded graph

title: nod-error-pages: 404 and error states held to the hero standard
description:
https://taskmaster.dev/nope renders naked browser-default text — '404' and 'Not Found' at 16px, top-left, no wordmark, no route home, no voice. We built a designed empty state for the ready set and then left the one error page every visitor eventually hits completely undesigned.

The back of the fence is the real quality bar: the hero is a 9 and this is a 3, and that gap is what a careful reader notices.

Voice is the product's own — dry, precise, no apology and no joke. It should say what happened and offer the one thing worth doing (go to the ready set). The empty state in the READY section is the tone reference: 'That is a graph problem, not a work problem.'
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] 404 uses the page's own type, ground and rules, and inherits the current look
[ ] Carries the wordmark and a route back to /
[ ] Copy is in the product's voice — states the fact, offers the next move, does not joke
[ ] +error.svelte covers 500 as well, and says something true rather than 'Internal Error'
[ ] Both looks checked; text roles clear 4.5:1 in each
close_reason: +error.svelte 404/500 in product voice (e91b96d)

title: nod-own-favicon: the browser tab flies the Svelte logo
description:
src/lib/assets/favicon.svg is still the SvelteKit scaffold's Svelte logo, so every tab, bookmark and history entry for taskmaster.dev shows another framework's branding.

The tab is the most persistent brand surface the product owns, and it is currently plywood on the FRONT of the cabinet. Cheap to fix and embarrassing to leave.

The mark should read at 16px and work on both grounds — Paper cream and Graphite near-black. The design already has an obvious candidate: the ready pip. A single filled dot in the signal colour IS the product's whole idea (one thing is startable), and it survives being 16 pixels wide, which a wordmark will not.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Favicon is Taskmaster's own mark; no Svelte logo anywhere in the repo
[ ] Legible at 16px, and correct against both looks (it ships as one asset, so it cannot rely on either ground)
[ ] SVG, and the existing per-look theme-color meta still matches
close_reason: favicon is a #c8ff2f pip (edf8c69)

title: nod-eyebrow-copy: '6 nodes resolved' is the wrong word and the wrong number
description:
The hero eyebrow reads 'intention bazaar-lgr · 6 nodes resolved'. Nothing was resolved — that is the word for a dependency being satisfied, not for a node existing — and 6 is every node in the graph including closed ones, which makes it a count of nothing in particular.

Small, but it is the first line of text under the wordmark and it currently means nothing on inspection. The rest of the page is scrupulous about saying only true things; this line is not carrying its weight.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] The eyebrow states something true and checkable
[ ] The number, if kept, is a quantity a reader can verify against the ledger below
[ ] Reads correctly when the ready set is empty
close_reason: eyebrow is {ready.length} startable + as of (5907cb8)

title: nod-dev-noise: vite HMR errors on the public domain
description:
Every page load of https://taskmaster.dev logs three console errors: vite's HMR client trying to reach wss://taskmaster.dev/ (400 on handshake) and then wss://localhost:5173/ (SSL error).

Harmless to rendering, but it is dev-mode leaking onto the public face, and a console full of red is the first thing anyone technical checks. It also means HMR does not work through the public domain — a live-dev cost, not just cosmetics.

Fix is server.hmr config (clientPort / protocol / host) so the client points somewhere real, or disabling the HMR client for non-local hosts. Related: the app runs in dev mode on purpose (ARCHITECTURE), so 'just build it' is a different, larger decision — do not smuggle it in here.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Zero console errors on a cold load of https://taskmaster.dev
[ ] HMR still works for local development against the guest
[ ] Still dev mode; no adapter/build change smuggled in
close_reason: HMR client skipped on taskmaster.dev hostname (0d8b9c6)
